Class CausalDependencies

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalDependencies
public final class CausalDependencies extends Object
A producer-stamped set of causal requirements: the positions a consumer must have observed before a record stamped with these dependencies may be delivered.

The usual flow at a topology edge is to hold a running CausalDependencies as your own causal frontier: start from using(CausalTopics) to bind a resolver, fold in each record you consume with observe(ConsumerRecord) — which accumulates the upstream's dependencies and the consumed record's own position — then attach the result to each outbound record with stamp(ProducerRecord). A one-to-one relay is using(topics).observe(record); a fan-in chains an observe per input. To assert a dependency you did not consume, build one with builder(CausalTopics). Serialise with toBytes() / fromBytes(byte[]).

The serialised form is 5 + 28 × coordinates bytes. An instance spanning many partitions can breach Kafka's record-size limit (message.max.bytes, ~1 MB by default); the figure to watch is a wide-fan-in record that depends on many topic-partitions.

    • empty

      public static CausalDependencies empty()
      Returns an empty instance with no positions recorded and no resolver bound. To accumulate dependencies from consumed records, prefer using(CausalTopics), which binds a resolver so observe(ConsumerRecord) needs no per-call topics argument.
      Returns:
      an empty CausalDependencies

    • using

      public static CausalDependencies using(CausalTopics topics)
      Returns an empty instance bound to topics, ready to accumulate consumed records with observe(ConsumerRecord). This is the start of the consumer-side frontier chain: bind the resolver once here, then observe(record) each record you consume without repeating topics. The bound resolver flows through observe(ConsumerRecord) and merge(CausalDependencies), but is never serialised and never affects equality.
      Parameters:
      topics - the resolver mapping topic names to their Kafka UUIDs; must not be null
      Returns:
      an empty CausalDependencies bound to topics

    • merge

      public CausalDependencies merge(CausalDependencies other)
      Returns the causal union of these dependencies and other — the per-coordinate maximum offset. Use this to combine the dependencies of several consumed records before stamping a fan-in record.
      Parameters:
      other - the dependencies to merge in; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new CausalDependencies dominating both inputs

    • observe

      public CausalDependencies observe(org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecord<?,?> record)
      Folds a consumed record into these dependencies and returns the result: the union of these dependencies, the dependencies record itself carried, and record's own position (topic, partition, offset).

      This is the consumer-side frontier accumulator. A node consuming with a plain Kafka client has no Parsley engine maintaining a frontier for it, so it maintains one here: bind a resolver once with using(CausalTopics), observe(record) every record you consume, and stamp the result onto every record you produce, so downstream consumers wait until they have observed everything this node did. A one-to-one relay is CausalDependencies.using(topics).observe(record); a fan-in (an output caused by several inputs) chains an observe per input; a stateful node whose output reflects everything it has consumed keeps a single instance and observes into it across records. Repeated positions on a coordinate take the maximum offset, so re-observing is safe.

      Requires a resolver to be bound — created via using(CausalTopics) or builder(CausalTopics), or carried through a prior observe / merge.

      Parameters:
      record - the consumed record to fold in; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new CausalDependencies extended with record's past and own position
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no resolver is bound, or if record carries a malformed dependencies header
      IllegalArgumentException - if record's topic cannot be resolved to a UUID

    • stamp

      public <K,V> org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerRecord<K,V> stamp(org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerRecord<K,V> record)
      Returns a copy of record carrying these dependencies in its parsley-causal-dependencies header, ready to send through a plain Kafka producer. The input record is never mutated: a fresh header set is built (preserving every other header), and stamping is idempotent — any existing dependencies header is replaced, not duplicated.
      Type Parameters:
      K - the record key type
      V - the record value type
      Parameters:
      record - the record to stamp; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new ProducerRecord with the dependencies header attached
